title: Design Phone Directory
statement:
Build a class `PhoneDirectory` that manages a pool of phone numbers `0, 1, ..., maxNumbers - 1`. At the start every number is free.

- `PhoneDirectory(maxNumbers)` creates the directory with all `maxNumbers` numbers free.
- `get()` hands out one free number and returns it; from then on that number is taken. If every number is taken, it returns `-1`.
- `check(number)` returns `true` if `number` is free right now and `false` if it is taken.
- `release(number)` makes `number` free again so a later `get` can hand it out. Releasing a number that is already free does nothing.

When several numbers are free, `get` may return any one of them; every such choice is accepted.
constraints: At most 2 * 10^4 calls in total are made to get, check and release
notes:
## Intuition

The directory has to remember two things: which numbers are free (so `check` answers instantly) and which free number to hand out next (so `get` is instant too). The simplest idea, scanning for the first free number on every `get`, works but costs O(maxNumbers) per call. Instead keep every free number waiting in a queue: `get` takes the one at the front, and `release` puts a number back at the end. A boolean array next to the queue answers `check` and tells `release` whether the number really was taken.

## Approach

1. In the constructor, mark every number free in `isFree` and put `0 .. maxNumbers - 1` in `queue`. `front` is the index of the next number to hand out.
2. `get()`: if `front` has reached the end of `queue`, nothing is free, so return `-1`.
3. Otherwise take `queue[front]`, move `front` forward, mark the number taken and return it.
4. `check(number)`: return `isFree[number]`.
5. `release(number)`: if the number is already free, stop. Otherwise mark it free and push it onto the end of `queue`.

## Example 1, step by step

With `maxNumbers = 3`, `queue = [0, 1, 2]` and `front = 0`. `get` returns `0`, then `1` (`front = 2`). `check(2)` finds `isFree[2] = true`. `get` returns `2`, so `check(2)` is now `false`. `release(2)` marks it free and appends it, making `queue = [0, 1, 2, 2]` with `front = 3`, and `check(2)` is `true` again. Output: `[null, 0, 1, true, 2, false, null, true]`.

## Complexity

- Time: the constructor is O(maxNumbers); `get`, `check` and `release` are O(1) each.
- Space: O(maxNumbers + r), where r is the number of successful releases; the slots before `front` are never read again.

## Pitfalls

- Releasing a number that is already free must not add it to the queue a second time, or a later `get` could hand out the same number twice.
- `Array.prototype.shift` is O(n) in JavaScript; moving a `front` index keeps `get` O(1).
- `get` must return `-1` only when no number is free at all, including after releases have refilled the queue.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `isFree` | `isFree[number]` is `true` while that number is not handed out |
| `queue` | the free numbers waiting to be handed out (from `front` onward) |
| `front` | index in `queue` of the next number `get` returns |
| `number` | the phone number being handed out, checked or released |
